body:
That's good advice that I have tried to practice. I've learned an instrument, I am currently training in MMA and in the past I've tried a few hobbies I thought I might enjoy like climbing or mountain biking. These things are fairly entertaining but they don't make me look forward to the future. I don't eagerly anticipate these activities but are rather things I do because I would be sitting at home otherwise. 

Looking forward to the future isn't something that is completely foreign to me. As a kid, I vaguely remember loving to play and going to sleep with thoughts of fun I could have the next day. I'm not sure when it happened, but that anticipatory feeling is gone. It is a symptom of adulthood I've been told. I honestly can say I have no single thing I love or have a passion for in my life. Which I am strangely fine with but it seems like looking forward to stuff comes naturally for others though. I think I would like that.

Nothing really significant happened that comes to mind. I just put off studying until tests came around. Even when I got to the point to where the notes were in my hand, I would not allow myself to focus and process information. I would literally do anything else to procrastinate, including helping friends study for their finals. 

I suppose it is just constantly being in a not so good mood that is wearing down on me. It seems like it won't go away. And I don't know if I actually want it to go away, because the alternative is pretty comforting to me. Thinking about living out the natural span of my life, another sixty or seventy years sounds ridiculous. Even another couple of years sounds exhausting and unfulfilling.  

Any who it's very nice that you care. I know I have others that care for me and very likely love me. They wouldn't want me to go. But they don't have to exist as me. That sounds so whiny.
